_source: Static UI keys for the mobile site goods-receipt review (route field-gr, pototype/mobile-screens.jsx MFieldGR L364-423). KEYS ONLY — never a translation. ZERO-MINT: all three values are keys that ALREADY EXIST in docs/extract/i18n-full.json today, so this slice touches the sacred file not at all and spends none of a Wei sacred round (the st_receive precedent; BLOCKERS.md B-266 warns that minting copy which can never be backed wastes a round permanently). ELEVEN prototype strings have no honest key in any layer and are therefore NOT rendered by this screen and NOT invented here — they are reported in BLOCKERS.md B-324 for a mint round. The eleven, with what each would cost: the shortfall noun and 'partial' (L384, the per-line caption — replaced here by the signed shortfall QUANTITY in the prototype's own danger tone, which needs no copy); 'QC Checklist' and its four labels 'ของถูกต้องตาม PO' / 'สภาพไม่เสียหาย' / 'บรรจุภัณฑ์ครบ' / 'เอกสารใบส่งของแนบ' (L393-407 — the whole section is dropped, so these five would be minted for a section that has NO column, NO field and NO table to store a result in; they should be minted only if B-324 rules the QC surface into the backend first); 'รูปสินค้าที่รับ' (L409, the gallery title — dropped with its section); 'คืน/ปฏิเสธ' (L418) and 'เซ็นรับ GR' (L419), the two footer buttons; and the two halves of L373, 'ส่งของ {date}' and 'ใบส่ง {no}', whose underlying columns do not exist either. HIGHEST-VALUE MINT of the eleven is 'คืน/ปฏิเสธ' alone: its endpoint POST /gr/:id/return is REAL and atomic (gr.ts L727, B-156), so one phrase unblocks one working action — everything else needs schema work first.
_deviations: ONE copy under-claim, and it is an existing key that says LESS than the prototype rather than an invented string that says more. title = dict po.list.receiveGoods, whose th is BYTE-EXACT with the prototype's L367 title — the deviation is only that the key's path names the PO list screen, not this one; it is the same phrase for the same act on the same document family. NOT REUSED, deliberately, and each rejection was checked byte by byte against the sacred source this round: (1) the shortfall noun has TWO byte-exact dict matches, labor.att.optAbsent (th 'absent from work') and inv.status.out (th 'out of stock') — both read correctly in Thai today and would render a WRONG word the moment en/zh/ar are filled, which is the exact trap st_receive refused; (2) gr.list.shortReceived is the right sentence but HARDCODES a single unit inside its own value, so it would print a bar-unit shortfall on a bag line (the seed's first line is in bags); (3) gr.create.partialCheckbox merely CONTAINS 'Partial' inside a different string; (4) common.reject is byte-exact for the second half of the return/reject button but drops the FIRST half — the half that names what POST /gr/:id/return actually does — so it would misdescribe an irreversible action rather than under-claim it; (5) gr.list.kpiReturns carries the right words for that same button but is a KPI-TILE id, which a translator would fill as the noun 'Returns'; (6) gr.create.attachBtn merely CONTAINS the gallery's noun inside a different string; (7) gr.create.deliveryNoteNo ('delivery note NUMBER') over-claims against L373's bare 'delivery note'. The empty state and the absent-value slots carry NO copy at all — an em-dash, the pm_close precedent — rather than borrowing a near-miss to fill a blank screen.
title: po.list.receiveGoods
